subject: Get a parameter estimate table from a lavaan.mi object?

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Get a parameter estimate table from a lavaan.mi object?
parts:
Dear All,

I would like to ask a quick question on runMI() and lavaan.mi class objects.

parameterEstimates() can be used to get the parameter estimates of the output of lavaan() and its wrappers in the form of a lavaan.data.frame object.

I found that parameterEstimates() does not work on a lavaan.mi object. Only lhs, op, and rhs is returned, as shown in the example below.

However, if I call summary() but output is not set to "text", the default, then, the output is a lavaan.data.frame, as shown below. I also compared the results with those from summary() with output = "text" and confirmed that results are the same.

Is this an intended behavior of the summary-method of lavaan.mi? Can I trust this way to use summary() as the lavaan.mi version of parameterEstimates()?

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)

The long example appended below:
# Adapted from the example of runMI()

library(semTools)
#> Loading required package: lavaan
#> This is lavaan 0.6-15
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
#> 
#> ###############################################################################
#> This is semTools 0.5-6
#> All users of R (or SEM) are invited to submit functions or ideas for functions.
#> ###############################################################################
HSMiss <- HolzingerSwineford1939[ , c(paste("x", 1:9, sep = ""),
                                      "ageyr","agemo","school")]
set.seed(12345)
HSMiss$x5 <- ifelse(HSMiss$x5 <= quantile(HSMiss$x5, .3), NA, HSMiss$x5)
age <- HSMiss$ageyr + HSMiss$agemo/12
HSMiss$x9 <- ifelse(age <= quantile(age, .3), NA, HSMiss$x9)
HS.model <- '
  visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
  speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'
out1 <- cfa.mi(HS.model, data = HSMiss, m = 20, seed = 12345,
               miArgs = list(noms = "school"))

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Get a parameter estimate table from a lavaan.mi object?
parts: parameterEstimates() can be used to get the parameter estimates of the output of lavaan() and its wrappers in the form of a lavaan.data.frame object.
The latter is its class (inherits from data.frame), not a wrapper function.  The special class is just so lavaan can define a nicer print method than the default one for data.frame objects.
parameterEstimates() does not work on a lavaan.mi object.

No, that is not a generic function, so I can't write a method for it to operate on lavaan.mi objects.  lavaan will allow parameterEstimates() to be applied to a class?lavaanList object, which is what lavaan.mi inherits from, but it is not informative.
Is this an intended behavior of the summary-method of lavaan.mi? Can I trust this way to use summary() as the lavaan.mi version of parameterEstimates()?

Yes, the lavaan.mi analog is just the summary() method (which is a generic function).  To make it return a familiar data.frame like parameterEstimates() does, just set the argument output = "data.frame" (see class?lavaan.mi).  
lavaan's summary() method also just calls parameterEstimates(..., output = "text"), but will return it in a list with anything else you request (e.g., fitMeasures() or modindices(), by setting the corresponding arguments TRUE).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Thanks a lot for the detailed explanation and sorry for my oversight. I was studying the help page of lavaan.mi class when I received your post. I should have read it first before posting.

It would be nice if commonly used lavaan functions can be used directly on lavaan.mi objects, or raise an error when a function should not be used on lavaan.mi objects, but I understand this may not be desirable. Changes may need to be made in lavaan, as in the case of parameterEstimates(). For personal use, I am compiling a list of functions that I usually use on lavaan objects (I do not use lavaanList objects) and see whether and/or how these functions work on lavaan.mi objects.

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)
